messages:
anne: Quick proposal — we need a head-to-head benchmark that isolates kernel selection and KV priming effects on scale-up time and burst credit consumption. current repo tests mix too many variables, so we can't tell if regressions are from batching heuristics or kernel choices.

dan: +1. Can you sketch the experiment? short bursts? long ramp?

ande: sorry typo — anne meant 'anne'.
maria: idea: run 3x scenarios per model: (1) synthetic steady QPS, (2) replay harness with cold-prefixes, (3) replay with primed KV cache. compare p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, and burst credits consumed.

anne: exactly. proposal details:
- models: gpt-small-quant, gpt-medium-fp16
- kernels: default auto (heuristic), force-int8-kernel, force-fp16-kernel
- batching: default runtime batching vs fixed small batch (1-4) vs aggressive batch (16)
- priming: no-priming, small-priming (50 sample prefixes), full-priming (replay full warmed traces)
- traffic: 2 minute cold start spike to 500 qps, then sustained 60s at 250 qps, then drop to 10 qps
- targets: measure scale-up latency (time to reach 90% of steady throughput), p95 latency, KV miss ratio, and burst credits used

leo: add: record kernel selection logs and the kernel decision reason (latency vs throughput) from runtime; we saw kernel flips mid-run in last perf job.

maria: also capture KV cache occupancy over time + per-GPU KV eviction counts. those explain token inflation when priming isn't complete.

dan: bench command draft (feel free to iterate):
```
bench-run --mode=replay --trace=customer-sample-042 --models="gpt-small-quant,gpt-medium-fp16" \
  --kernels="auto,int8,fp16" --batching="fixed:1-4,aggressive:16" \
  --priming="none,50,full" --spike=500:120 --sustain=250:60 --cool=10:60 \
  --outputs="latency,p95,tokens_per_s,kv_miss,burstcredits,kernellog" --outdir=/tmp/bench-1876
```

anne: perfect. bench-bot can kick off matrix runs if we upload parameters. bench-bot: can you queue the matrix with 3 warmup runs each? @bench-bot

bench-bot: queued 18 jobs (3 models x 3 kernels x 2 batching x 3 priming = 54 actually, running in batches). scheduling across dedicated test pool "dedicated-bench-1". estimated time ~6h. posting run ids when jobs start. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

leo: question on dedicated pool: do we want to test with and without burst credits enabled on the pool? last time dedicated pools hidden burstcredits altered behavior.

maria: yes include both. one set where pool has burst credits enabled, another with strict SLO (no burst). compare how runtime degrades and if fallback kernels trigger earlier.

dan: regarding metrics: let's add kernel switch count and reason to the dashboard widget. if we see frequent mid-request kernel jumps that's bad.

anne: agreed. action items:
- maria: add KV occupancy + eviction logging to bench harness (low-overhead counters).
- leo: ensure kernel decision traces are on and sampled at 1/10 requests.
- dan: add dashboard panels and an apples-to-thing comparison csv export (head-to-head CSV).
- anne: coordinate with bench-bot and commit the run matrix and link the run ids in this thread when available.

maria: will PR small counters today. i'll also attach a short doc on how priming levels map to expected KV hit rates.

leo: note: be careful with synthetic traffic config — use inter-arrival distribution we recorded from real customer trace, not pure poisson. synthetic-poisson exaggerates batching and hides kernel mis-routing.

anne: good call. use replay-derived inter-arrival.

bench-bot: job 1876543210-01 started on dedicated-bench-1 (kernels=auto,model=gpt-small-quant,priming=none,batching=fixed). logs: https://bench.internal/runs/1876543210-01

dan: thanks. once a few runs finish let's convene quick triage to see if we need to tweak warmup length for priming. 30m meeting?

anne: let's do 30m after first three jobs complete. ping here when bench-bot posts completion ids.

maria: PR up: +kv counters, small sampling. link: https://git.company/bench/priming-counters (will link commit in run metadata).

leo: tiny nit — call the CSV export field "head_to_head_id" rather than apples or compare.

anne: updated. thanks all.

bench-bot: job 1876543210-01 completed. summary: scale-up latency=18s to 90%, p95=210ms at steady, burstcredits used=12. artifacts uploaded.

anne: great start — we'll comb results in triage.
